claim_text: Newly infiltrating NK -> dysfunctional tumour NK

audit.primary_source_citation: Liu VV, Sandor K, Yan PK, Miao Z, Yin Y, Stickels RR, Chen AY, Hiam-Galvez K, Gutierrez J, Zhang W, Sajjath SM, Valbuena R, Wang S, Daniel B, Ludwig LS, Howitt BE, Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell. 2026 Jul 13;44(7):1509-1521.e4. doi:10.1016/j.ccell.2026.05.006. PMID 42242233; PMC13309241. Preprint: bioRxiv 2025.07.16.665245 (posted 2025-07-21). HINT VERIFIED: the paper, first author (Vincent V. Liu), journal and year in the hint are all correct — this is a real paper, not a misremembered citation. It is a PRIMARY source (method development + primary human data), not a review. Dataset = GSE302113. NOTE: this paper is NOT about NK cells; its abstract, title and every stated conclusion concern MYELOID cells (monocyte->macrophage/DC3). The NK content is two sentences and a supplemental panel (Figure S6E / preprint S5E).
audit.species: Homo sapiens (primary source: patient tumour resections, non-involved lung tissue and peripheral blood). Counter-evidence/alternative sources audited are Mus musculus (Sojka 2014 parabiosis; Gasteiger 2015 parabiosis; Gao 2017 tumour models).
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, at a SINGLE cross-sectional timepoint (the moment of therapeutic lobectomy / debulking surgery — no time course, no follow-up sample, no longitudinal tracking), joint single-cell chromatin accessibility + mitochondrial-DNA genotype (mtscATAC-seq) was measured on freshly dissociated, UNCULTURED matched tumour, non-involved lung tissue (NILT) and PBMCs from 5 early-stage NSCLC patients (SU-L-001..005) and on matched tumour + PBMC from 5 ovarian cancer patients (SU-O-001..005). Cells were grouped into "clones" by shared low-frequency somatic mtDNA heteroplasmic variants (mgatk calls at <1% pseudobulk frequency; Mitotrek: variants in >20% of a donor's cells or in <3 cells removed; heteroplasmy matrix binarised at 0.07; variants linked into clonotypes by Pearson rho >0.5 across cells; cells assignable to >1 clone DISCARDED; chrM:307-314 homopolymer region excluded). The readout that bears on this claim is the tissue-site distribution of cells belonging to 14 PBMC-enriched clones (>=10 cells each), of which 2 were NK-dominated and came from ONE donor (SU-L-005). NK identity was assigned only by chromatin gene-accessibility score for GNLY/NCR1/KLRD1/CD3D-negative plus Azimuth PBMC-reference label transfer. NO functional or dysfunction readout of NK cells was performed anywhere in the paper — no cytotoxicity, no degranulation/CD107a, no IFN-gamma/TNF production, no inhibitory-receptor or "exhaustion" protein measurement, no TGF-beta-response assay — and the chromatin state of blood-resident versus tumour-resident members of the SAME NK clone was never compared. Verbatim preprint text (the only place the hinted numbers exist): "Among 14 peripheral blood-enriched clones, 10 were dominated by CD8+ T cells and 2 by NK cells from a single donor (SU-L-005). Although the majority of cells from these clones were detected in PBMCs (66.0%), smaller fractions were present in tumor (25.3%) and NILT (8.8%), indicating their ability to infiltrate tissue."
audit.n: NK-specific observation: n = 1 donor (SU-L-005), yielding 2 NK-dominated clones. Whole cohort: n = 5 NSCLC + 5 ovarian = 10 donors. (Cell counts, which are NOT the n: 218,715 cells total; 83,371 lung tumour+NILT, 41,587 lung PBMC, 52,154 ovarian tumour, 41,603 ovarian PBMC.)
audit.n_unit: donors (patients); secondary unit = mtDNA clones (2 NK-dominated, out of 14 blood-enriched, out of ~200+ called clones)
audit.controls: Internal patient-matched design (each donor is its own control: PBMC vs tumour vs NILT from the same person, same processing batch). Comparison clone classes: tumour-enriched and NILT-enriched clones, and the 186 non-enriched clones. Useful negative comparator: B/plasma-cell-dominated clones NEVER spanned blood, showing the assay does not force cross-compartment sharing. Method controls: Mitotrek benchmarked against published HSPC colony data with independently known clonal truth (91.3% and 85.3% assignment accuracy in 2 donors); for SU-O-002, orthogonal paired scRNA/TCR-seq on 6,982 cells showed TCR-mtDNA clonotype correspondence; variants >1% pseudobulk frequency excluded as zygotic/developmental; ArchR QC (TSS enrichment >4, >1000 unique fragments) and doublet scoring; multi-clone cells discarded; annotations cross-checked by Azimuth. The authors themselves flag two uncontrolled confounders specific to solid-tumour samples: ambient mtDNA uptake during single-cell capture and horizontal mitochondrial transfer, both of which "are unlikely to reflect bona fide clonal relationships." MISSING CONTROLS relevant to this claim: no non-cancer/healthy donor; no second timepoint; no per-compartment NK-capture-depth normalisation; no orthogonal directional tracer of any kind (no labelling, no transfer, no parabiosis, no intravascular staining); and no dysfunction assay against which a "dysfunctional" endpoint could be defined.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: THREE alternatives, each of which fully explains the data without any A->B transition. (1) PARALLEL SEEDING FROM A SHARED PROGENITOR (the canonical "pre-existing subset" alternative, and the strongest here). A shared somatic mtDNA variant proves shared ANCESTRY, not shared TRAJECTORY. A blood NK cell and a tumour NK cell in the same clone are exactly what you expect if a single bone-marrow HSPC/NK-progenitor clone independently exported progeny to blood and to tissue in parallel. The paper itself endorses precisely this reading for innate cells: innate populations show "high intra-group clone sharing, consistent with recent hematopoietic output without substantial clonal bottlenecks prior to tissue infiltration." A cross-sectional snapshot cannot distinguish parallel seeding from sequential conversion, and the study contains no directional information at all. (2) TECHNICAL / SAMPLING-DEPTH ARTEFACT, and this repo's own data makes it concrete. A clone is called "PBMC-enriched" by the relative fraction of its cells recovered per compartment, so the classification is directly confounded by how many NK cells were captured per compartment. Per /home/user/aaa/out/T4_power.tsv, SU-L-005 — the single donor that produced both NK-dominated blood-enriched clones — has 7,713 blood NK cells versus 446 tumour NK cells (17:1), and 3.7x more blood NK than the next-highest lung donor (SU-L-002, 1,488; others 707/803/2,065). The one donor most likely to yield blood-enriched NK clones purely by sampling depth is the one donor that did. Additionally, at a 0.07 binarisation threshold with clones built from single variants linked at rho>0.5, and a benchmarked assignment accuracy of only 85-91%, two clones in one donor sit inside the method's own error envelope; and the authors flag ambient-mtDNA uptake and horizontal mitochondrial transfer as tumour-specific sources of spurious linkage. (3) TWO INDEPENDENT ORIGINS. The intratumoural dysfunctional NK compartment may be a distinct pre-existing tissue-resident lineage (CD49a+ trNK / ILC1-like) that never transited blood, selected and expanded locally, coexisting with a separate recirculating cNK pool that transits the tumour without converting. Sojka 2014 (parabiosis, mouse) establishes exactly this two-lineage structure in liver, uterus and skin: CD49a+DX5- trNK stay host-restricted while CD49a-DX5+ cNK equilibrate between parabionts. Note finally that even if alternative (1)-(3) were all excluded, the claim would still be unevidenced, because the "-> dysfunctional" half of the claim was never measured by any assay in this paper.
audit.counter_evidence: SEARCHED AND FOUND. (a) Sojka DK et al., eLife 2014;3:e01659, PMID 24714492 / PMC3975579 — REAL parabiosis (CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic pairs, 2 weeks post-surgery, spleen reaching near-complete chimerism as internal control). Verbatim: "In both the uterus and skin, host CD49a+ DX5- NK cells were primarily found in the indicated host tissue... the CD49a- DX5+ NK cells of both allotypes were found in both parabionts, indicating that they were circulating NK cells." Direct support for a pre-existing, non-blood-derived tissue-resident NK lineage; direct counter to a universal blood-NK->tissue-NK conversion model. Mouse, non-tumour. (b) Gasteiger G et al., Science 2015;350:981-5, PMID 26472762 / PMC4720139 — parabiosis: ILCs "are tissue-resident cells that were maintained and expanded locally," with hematogenous replenishment only partial and only at late timepoints after infection. Local self-renewal, not blood recruitment. (c) The primary source's OWN only NK-specific positive finding is a SELECTION/EXPANSION result, not a conversion result: "we observed oligoclonal NK cell expansions in one ovarian tumor (SU-O-005), consistent with adaptive-like NK responses reported in other contexts." That is the canonical alternative (a pre-existing clone expands in situ) appearing inside the same paper. Do not conflate SU-O-005 (ovarian, oligoclonal expansion) with SU-L-005 (lung, blood-enriched NK clones) — different donors, different cohorts, different findings. (d) INTEGRITY FINDING on the field's flagship "NK becomes dysfunctional in tumour" paper: Gao Y et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:1004-15 (PMID 28759001, TGF-beta-driven NK->intILC1->ILC1 conversion) carries a 2024 Author Correction (PMID 38514890, doi 10.1038/s41590-024-01799-9) stating that Figures 5e and 6d,e and Supplementary Figures 5c,d and 8c "were based on experiments for which no evidence of their conduct or primary data could be confirmed... the data from the underlying experiments are believed to have been fabricated or are unreliable," following a QIMR Berghofer investigation; the panels were removed. The correction asserts the main TGF-beta/ILC1 conclusion is unaffected, but any downstream reliance on Gao 2017 for a mouse conversion result must be flagged. Separately, Gao 2017 concerns NK->ILC1 within the TME and does NOT establish that the converting cells were newly arrived from blood — it is not evidence for X2 as stated. (e) SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND (this is a finding, not an absence of search): I ran targeted searches for a tumour-transplant or parabiosis mouse experiment tracking blood NK recruitment into a tumour and acquisition of a dysfunctional state, and for Kaede/photoconversion or intravascular-staining NK tumour-infiltration experiments. No such primary experiment surfaced; every hit was a review. I could not locate it — I am not asserting it does not exist.
audit.downstream_dependency: CONCRETE AND NAMED: /home/user/aaa/scripts/phaseC_power.py lines 162-163 — verdict("X2 blood vs tumour (lung)", ("blood","tumour"), lung) and verdict("X2 blood vs tumour (ovarian)", ("blood","tumour"), ovar) — the preregistered X2 feasibility/power gate (constants at lines 34-36: MIN_NK=30 NK cells per compartment, MIN_DONORS=3, MIN_COV=20.0x chrM). It runs over GSE302113, which IS the Liu et al. dataset audited here, and writes /home/user/aaa/out/T4_power.tsv. Current state of that file: the lung arm PASSES with 4 donors (SU-L-001, -002, -004, -005; SU-L-003 fails because its tumour has 0 NK cells), and the ovarian arm FAILS with 1 donor (only SU-O-005 clears >=30 NK in both blood and tumour, versus MIN_DONORS=3). Two consequences follow from this audit. First, the planned phaseC X2 re-analysis is NOT independent replication — it re-interrogates the same 10 donors, the same mtDNA variants and the same clone calls that produced the original supplemental observation, so a "confirmation" there would be circular. Second, and more actionable: the SU-L-005 NK capture imbalance documented in that same T4_power.tsv (7,713 blood NK vs 446 tumour NK) is the specific confounder that generated the blood-enriched NK clones in the first place, so any phaseC X2 verdict must be depth-matched or downsampled per compartment before a blood-vs-tumour clone-sharing statistic is read as biology. Nothing else in the repo currently assumes X2 is TRUE (it is a screen target, not a premise), which is why this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: UPHOLDS the initial call for the claim AS STATED, and refines it in both directions. UPHOLD: the "-> dysfunctional tumour NK" half of X2 has ZERO evidence of any class in the primary source or in anything I found. Liu et al. never measured NK function or dysfunction in any compartment, never compared the state of blood-side versus tumour-side members of the same NK clone, and drew no NK conclusion in the abstract, title or discussion. So "ESSENTIALLY NO EVIDENCE" is correct for the claim as written. PARTIAL OVERTURN UPWARD: the hint's citation is real and its quotation is accurate, and what it points to is not nothing — it is a genuine somatic-mtDNA lineage barcode observation (OBS_GENETIC class, not marker similarity and NOT pseudotime/trajectory) placing blood-resident and tumour-resident NK cells in shared clones. For the strictly weaker proposition "blood and tumour NK cells can share clonal ancestry," there is real genetic evidence; a flat "no evidence" understates the class of data available. PARTIAL OVERTURN DOWNWARD — three specific corrections to the hint that make the evidence weaker than the hint implies: (i) The hint's framing "2 were NK-dominated in donor SU-L-005, with cells also found in tumour (25.3%) and NILT (8.8%)" MISATTRIBUTES the percentages. In the source, 66.0%/25.3%/8.8% is the AGGREGATE distribution across all 14 blood-enriched clones — of which 10 are CD8+ T-cell-dominated and only 2 are NK-dominated. The paper gives NO per-clone tissue breakdown for the 2 NK clones. The 25.3% tumour fraction is therefore dominated by CD8 T cells and cannot be attributed to NK cells at all. This is the single most important correction in this row. (ii) The numbers exist ONLY in the bioRxiv preprint (2025.07.16.665245). The peer-reviewed Cancer Cell version deleted them, the SU-L-005 attribution and the CD8/NK split, condensing the whole passage to: "A complementary analysis of PBMC-enriched clones identified 14 clones dominated by CD8+ T and NK cells, the majority of which were also detected at lower frequencies in tumor and NILT, indicating their capacity for tissue infiltration (Figure S6E)." Anyone citing the published paper for the hinted numbers is citing text that does not appear in it. (iii) n = 1 donor and 2 clones, in a supplemental panel, with the sampling-depth confound documented above from this repo's own T4_power.tsv. Additional hint correction: the hint asked about mouse tumour-transplant/parabiosis NK-recruitment experiments — I searched and did not find one; the parabiosis literature I did find (Sojka 2014, Gasteiger 2015) is non-tumour and points the OPPOSITE way, toward tissue residency and local self-renewal. Minor factual note: SU-L-005 is treatment-naive adenocarcinoma (SU-L-003 is the neuroendocrine case) — an intermediate web summary had this wrong; the primary text is authoritative. NET: the initial call survives, but "essentially no evidence" should be restated precisely as "OBS_GENETIC-class evidence, n=1 donor, for clonal ancestry shared between blood and tumour NK; no evidence of any class for directionality; no evidence of any class for the dysfunctional endpoint."
audit.methods_quote: CLONE DEFINITION (Cancer Cell STAR Methods, verbatim): "Clones are then called for each donor using mitotrek.core.assign_cell_to_clones. Variants present in >20% cells from a donor (likely technical or homoplasmic) or less than 3 cells are removed. The heteroplasmy matrix is then binarized with a cutoff of 0.07 based on the rationale that exact heteroplasmy levels are not reliable given the stochasticity from mitochondrial genome distribution during cell division and variance in per-cell mitochondrial genome coverage... To convert mitochondrial variants to clones, an undirected weighted graph is constructed in which vertices are variants and edges are defined by the Pearson correlation coefficient between two variants across cells, computed from the binarized heteroplasmy matrix. After removing edges with weights less than 0.5, each connected component in the graph was treated as a distinct clonotype." AUTHORS' OWN ARTEFACT CAVEAT (verbatim): "mtDNA variants detected at high allele frequencies in solid tissue cells were more frequently shared across cells, including from other lineages, than in matching PBMC samples, likely due to both technical artifacts (e.g., uptake of ambient mtDNA during single-cell capture) and biological phenomena (e.g., horizontal mitochondrial transfer events) that are unlikely to reflect bona fide clonal relationships and may be unique to solid tumor profiling." THE LOAD-BEARING RESULT (bioRxiv preprint, verbatim; deleted from the published version): "Our tumor-NILT enrichment analysis of immune clones implicitly excluded circulating immune cells that may have failed to infiltrate the lung tissues. To identify such clones, we assessed clone enrichment in PBMCs (Figure S5E). Among 14 peripheral blood-enriched clones, 10 were dominated by CD8+ T cells and 2 by NK cells from a single donor (SU-L-005). Although the majority of cells from these clones were detected in PBMCs (66.0%), smaller fractions were present in tumor (25.3%) and NILT (8.8%), indicating their ability to infiltrate tissue."
audit.notes: CLASSIFICATION RATIONALE (per G7, not loosened). I classify strongest = OBS_GENETIC because somatic mtDNA heteroplasmic variants are genuine heritable endogenous barcodes and this is real lineage tracing, benchmarked against ground-truth HSPC colonies and cross-validated against TCR clonotypes in one donor. But the class label attaches to a proposition strictly weaker than the claim: it observes SHARED CLONAL ANCESTRY at one timepoint, not a transition. It does not become OBS_DIRECT or OBS_TRANSFER, because nothing was tracked over time and nothing was transferred. INF_MARKER is listed second because the tumour-side "NK cell" is defined purely by chromatin gene-score plus reference projection, and the claim's endpoint ("dysfunctional") has no operational definition in the paper whatsoever. G2 CHECK: no pseudotime or RNA-velocity underlies this particular claim — Slingshot appears in the paper's reference list and is used for the MYELOID differentiation analysis, not for the NK/blood-enrichment result — so INF_TRAJECTORY is correctly absent here rather than suppressed. G5 CHECK: n is reported in donors (1 for the NK observation, 10 in the cohort), never in cells; the six-figure cell counts are explicitly labelled as not-the-n. G3 CHECK: every "not found" above is marked as searched-and-not-found with the queries recorded, never as does-not-exist. FULL TEXT: obtained and archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/X2_PMC13309241.txt (published Cancer Cell STAR Methods, from PMC13309241) and /home/user/aaa/refs/X2_biorxiv_preprint.txt + .pdf (53-page preprint containing the hinted numbers, which the published version deleted). Counter-evidence full text at /home/user/aaa/refs/X2_PMC3975579.txt (Sojka 2014, methods-confirmed parabiosis). Abstract-only records archived for PMID 28759001 (Gao 2017), 38514890 (its Author Correction) and 26472762 (Gasteiger 2015); the Gao correction's substance was obtained from the publisher-mirrored correction notice, not from the abstract. NOTE ON in_vivo FIELD: coded "in_vivo" because the clonal relationships arose in living patients and cells were profiled directly ex vivo without culture, but there was no in vivo manipulation, perturbation or tracking of any kind — this is an observational human-tissue snapshot, and the "in_vivo" label should not be read as implying an in vivo experiment. CONCRETE HANDOFF FOR PHASE C: before the X2 blood-vs-tumour clone-sharing statistic is computed on GSE302113, downsample or depth-match NK cells per compartment per donor; SU-L-005's 17:1 blood:tumour NK ratio (7,713 vs 446, per out/T4_power.tsv) is sufficient on its own to manufacture "blood-enriched" NK clones in that donor, and SU-L-005 is the sole donor behind the entire NK observation being audited.

adv.challenge_reason:
UPGRADE OVERALL, VIA A WRONG-PRIMARY-SOURCE CORRECTION, WITH A SIMULTANEOUS DOWNGRADE OF THE SOURCE THE AUDITOR ACTUALLY USED. Two separate verdicts, both from methods I read myself.

(1) DOWNGRADE of the audited source: Liu 2026 supports NOTHING about X2, and OBS_GENETIC is wrong for it. I re-ran `lit.py methods 42242233 --tag X2adv` (returns ABSTRACT_ONLY; no PMCID resolved) and read the archived STAR Methods (refs/X2_PMC13309241.txt) and the preprint (refs/X2_biorxiv_preprint.txt) line by line. Three defects, the last two NEW:
(a) The auditor granted OBS_GENETIC to the proposition "blood and tumour NK share clonal ancestry." That proposition is NOWHERE IN THE PAPER. Published line 200 reads only: "A complementary analysis of PBMC-enriched clones identified 14 clones dominated by CD8+ T and NK cells, the majority of which were also detected at lower frequencies in tumor and NILT (Figure S6E)." The preprint's 66.0/25.3/8.8% is an AGGREGATE over all 14 clones, 10 of which are CD8-dominated. There is no per-clone breakdown for the 2 NK clones anywhere in either version. Whether either NK clone contained a single tumour cell is unstated.
(b) NEW — the load-bearing panel is unverifiable and its legend is corrupt. Supplemental figures are absent from PMC. In the preprint, the Supplemental Figure 5 legend runs (A),(B),(C) and then a block "(D and E) Heatmaps showing the fraction of all cell pairs belonging to the same clone... within ovarian tumor (E) and PBMC (F)" — a VERBATIM DUPLICATE of the Supplemental Figure 6 (A and B) legend. The preprint therefore carries NO legend describing the panel (S5E) that the text cites for the NK result. I could not obtain the figure image. G3: searched, not obtainable — not asserting it is wrong.
(c) NEW AND DECISIVE — the "PBMC-enriched" call is a COMPOSITIONAL ARTEFACT of a mis-specified null, quantifiable from this repo's own data. Methods, verbatim: enrichment is "Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted Fisher's exact test against overall tissue site distribution." The null is the ALL-CELL-TYPE site marginal, not a cell-type-matched baseline. So any clone dominated by a cell type whose own site distribution differs from the all-cell marginal is flagged enriched with zero clonal biology. Computed from /home/user/aaa/out/T4_power.tsv: in SU-L-005 the NK-only site distribution is blood 79.3% / NILT 16.1% / tumour 4.6% against an all-cell marginal of blood 44.3% / NILT 33.1% / tumour 22.6% — a 1.79x blood enrichment and 0.20x tumour depletion built into composition alone. SU-L-005 has the largest blood-NK compositional skew and the lowest tumour NK fraction (3.8%) of any lung donor, and it is the sole donor that produced blood-enriched NK clones. The mirror image confirms it: SU-O-005 has NK compositional ratio 1.90x TOWARD tumour, and is precisely the donor where the paper reports "oligoclonal NK cell expansions in one ovarian tumor (SU-O-005)". Two opposite "findings" in two donors both fall out of per-donor NK composition. The prior auditor's "sampling depth" framing understates this: it is a deterministic per-donor prediction, not a noise argument.
(d) NEW — the skew is partly SORT DESIGN. FACS methods, verbatim: "Cells were classified into T cells (CD45+CD3+), other leukocytes (CD45+CD3-), and malignant or stromal cells (CD45-CD3-)." Per T4_power.tsv the gates differ by donor AND compartment: SU-L-005 blood = 2 libraries sorted CD3+/CD3- (the CD3- library is NK-enriched with no CD45- dilution) while SU-L-005 tumour = CD45+CD3+ and CD45+CD3-/CD45- (NK pooled with malignant and stromal cells); SU-L-003 blood was sorted CD56+/CD56- — explicit NK enrichment — while its tumour was unsorted "ALL" and yielded 0 NK.
G2 applied consistently forces the downgrade: single-timepoint mtDNA clone-sharing cannot distinguish "A becomes B" from "A and B are independently derived from a common ancestor", exactly as pseudotime cannot. mtDNA heteroplasmy is a CLONE label, not a STATE label, and it is inherited from an ancestor upstream of both compartments. For Liu 2026 the strongest class bearing on X2 is INF_MARKER (chromatin gene-score + Azimuth PBMC-reference label transfer, plus a compositionally confounded enrichment statistic). G2 check on Liu: Slingshot is used, but only for the MYELOID trajectory ("Corroboration via transcriptomic analyses"), so INF_TRAJECTORY is correctly absent — the prior auditor had this right.

(2) UPGRADE of the claim: the auditor missed the actual primary source, which is far stronger. Dean I, Lee CYC, ... Withers DR, "Rapid functional impairment of natural killer cells following tumor entry limits anti-tumor immunity," Nat Commun 2024;15:683, PMID 38267402 / PMC10808449. Its title IS claim X2. Full OA text with methods was ALREADY ARCHIVED IN THIS REPO at /home/user/aaa/refs/R2_PMC10808449.txt, and /home/user/aaa/phaseA/R2.json explicitly flags it as "the substance of X2/T4". The auditor's own log records "SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND ... Kaede/photoconversion" — I reproduce that negative (my PubMed query "photoconversion Kaede NK cell tumor" also returned 0), so the index genuinely fails here; the repo's own audit graph was the better index.
WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED (methods, not abstract): In Mus musculus, in vivo, MC38 colon adenocarcinoma grafted s.c. into C57BL/6 Kaede photoconvertible mice; at day 12-13 post-engraftment the tumour ALONE (rest of animal shielded with black MDF) was exposed to 405 nm focused LED, 9 cycles x 20 s, irreversibly converting all cells then inside the tumour Green->Red; mice sacrificed at 5 h, 24 h, 48 h or 72 h. Kaede-Green+ intratumoural NK = entered AFTER the label (newly infiltrating); Kaede-Red+ = present at t0. Readouts on CD3-NK1.1+ cells: integrin phenotype by flow (5 h: KG+ NK overwhelmingly CD11b+CD49a-, CD49a+ compartment ABSENT; 24 h: ~10% of KG+ are CD49a+; 72 h: KR+ essentially all CD49a+CD11b-); function measured on the time-stamped cells — CCL5 restricted to KG+CD11b+CD49a-, granzyme A high in CD11b+CD49a- and significantly lower in CD49a+, perforin significantly reduced in CD11b-CD49a+, CD107a significantly reduced among KR+, IFN-gamma significantly lower than splenic NK and Ifng-cre/mKate2 reporter negative in fresh intratumoural NK; granzyme B and C UP in KR+CD49a+; direct 4 h killing of B16-F10-Ova by FACS-sorted CD11b+ vs CD49a+ tumour NK at 1:10/1:20/1:40 E:T (CD11b+ significantly better).
n and n_unit (G5): n = MICE. Photoconversion time course 5 h n=5, 24 h n=8, 72 h n=11 (24/72 h pooled from 2 independent repeats); scRNA-seq UMAPs 24 h n=5, 72 h n=8; CCL5/IFN-gamma n=5; granzyme/perforin panel n=8 pooled from 2 experiments, CD107a n=5; killing assay n=3; MC38 vs MC38 Ptgs-/- n=4 vs 4; NK-HIF1alpha KO n=5 vs cre-negative littermates n=7. Human arm n=10 CRC patients (paired blood/unaffected colon/tumour flow). Legend note: "n = 3 refers to 3 mice each with a single tumor" — cells are never the n.
CONTROLS: (i) EGRESS EXCLUDED — tumours photoconverted, KR+ cells sought in dLN and spleen at 24/72 h, proportion and number very low and mostly CD49a-negative; (ii) INPUT-POPULATION CONTROL excluding the pre-existing subset — MACS-isolated splenic Kaede NK (CD49a-negative) transferred i.v. (2.5x10^5, day 12) into WT C57BL/6 MC38-bearing hosts, analysed 3 days later: transferred KG+ NK upregulated CD49a and granzyme C ONLY within MC38 tumours; (iii) circulating NK reference (public 10x mouse PBMC) mapped to NK_1/NK_2 and NONE to NK_5, Itga1 absent from circulating NK; (iv) tumour NK phenotypically distinct from ILC1 in spleen/liver/small intestine/colon; (v) cross-model replication in CT26 (s.c. and orthotopic colonic wall), B16-F10-OVA, EO771 orthotopic mammary, MMTV-PyMT primary, 4T1; (vi) mechanism perturbations all negative or partial — anti-OX40 Treg depletion no effect on integrins, MC38 Ptgs1/2-/- partial, Ncr1-iCre x Hif1a-fl/fl conditional HIF-1alpha deletion no effect.
REVISED CLASSIFICATION: strongest = OBS_DIRECT (in vivo site-specific irreversible temporal fate-labelling with defined t0 and 5/24/48/72 h chase, state read on time-stamped cells). Also present: OBS_TRANSFER (splenic Kaede NK -> tumour-bearing host, an independent second observation of the same transition); INF_INVITRO (TGF-beta/PGE2 and 1% O2 cultures; 4 h killing assay); INF_MARKER (CD49a/CD11b gating as the state definition; the entire human CRC arm); INF_TRAJECTORY (Monocle pseudotime + PAGA rooted BY HAND in NK_1 + SCENIC over pseudotime). G2 DISCIPLINE: Dean's pseudotime is real and must be listed, but the directional claim does NOT rest on it — it rests on the photo-label, an independent physical clock, and the 24/72 h time-stamped data are PROJECTED onto the trajectory to validate it, not the reverse. G7 DISCIPLINE: I do NOT count OBS_GENETIC for the lineage claim. Ncr1-iCre x Hif1a-fl/fl and Ifng-cre/mKate2 are mechanism and reporter tools, not fate maps of the A->B transition; Kaede is a photoconvertible protein, not a recombination-based fate map. Calling those OBS_GENETIC would be exactly the loosening G7 forbids.
WHAT STILL DOES NOT SURVIVE, so the upgrade is not oversold: (i) the fate mapping is MOUSE and in transplantable syngeneic lines; Dean's human arm is cross-sectional flow on n=10 CRC patients plus reanalysis of 3,521 NK cells from 62 patients = INF_MARKER, no human fate mapping; (ii) "dysfunctional" is a state SWITCH, not uniform loss — granzyme A, perforin, CD107a, CCL5, IFN-gamma down but granzyme B and granzyme C UP; (iii) the photo-label marks "not in tumour at t0", which includes NK in other tissues, not blood specifically — only the i.v. transfer arm addresses blood origin; (iv) the residual alternative is NOT excluded (see counter-evidence).

adv.new_counter_evidence:
SIX items the prior auditor missed, five of them primary and three functional.

(1) THE CANONICAL ALTERNATIVE SURVIVES INSIDE DEAN 2024 ITSELF — SELECTIVE DEATH PLUS IN SITU EXPANSION. Dean state the CD49a-negative KR+ cells "must all either differentiate to a CD49a+ state, egress the tumor, or die in situ." They tested egress and excluded it. They did NOT test death in situ. No viability dye timecourse, no BrdU/EdU, no Bcl2 or caspase readout on the KG+CD11b+ compartment. And their own data supplies the expansion half: "NK_5 was particularly enriched among the cycling NK cells, suggesting that some tumor-retained NK cells may expand in situ." A model in which newly arrived CD11b+ NK are selectively deleted while a small CD49a+ pool proliferates reproduces every reported proportion without any conversion. This is the strongest surviving alternative and it is a genuine gap, not a technicality — the transfer arm blunts it (splenic input was CD49a-negative) but is a single 3-day readout with no dose-response.

(2) Buggert/Bjorkstrom et al., "Transient tissue residency and lymphatic egress define human CD56bright NK cell homeostasis," Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907 — OA full text fetched and read (refs/X2adv_PMC12571907.txt). This is the human gold-standard method for X2's exact structural question and cuts both ways. HLA-MISMATCHED HUMAN LIVER TRANSPLANTATION with sampling at t=0 h, 6 h and 1 YEAR, donor vs recipient cells separated by HLA-allele staining, plus intravascular labelling, humanized mice, non-human primates and efferent lymph cannulation. Verbatim: "donor-derived CD56bright NK cells represent the dominant TR NK cell population early after transplantation, but are replaced over time by infiltrating recipient NK cells that establish TR traits, a process partly regulated by Runx3." SUPPORTS the general mechanism in humans in vivo. But it DAMAGES X2's "blood-derived" premise in two ways: "CD56dim NK cells, constrained to vasculature at steady state" — the dominant cytotoxic subset, and the one that dominates tumour infiltrates, does not freely access tissue at steady state; and residency is TRANSIENT with lymphatic recirculation, contradicting a terminal tumour-retained endpoint and contradicting Dean's mouse egress-exclusion when carried to humans.

(3) Serger C et al., Sci Immunol 2026;11(120):eaeb6645, PMID 42247486 — same disease (NSCLC), same tissue (lung tumour) as Liu 2026, and it inverts X2's endpoint. Intratumoural NK are dominated by two taNK subsets marked by ITGAE (CD103) and ITGA1 (CD49a) that "display features of tissue residency and dysfunction WHILE PRESERVING CYTOTOXIC FUNCTION"; CD39+ taNK are "the dominant cytotoxic NK cell population with superior killing capacity." The cells that look dysfunctional by marker are the MOST cytotoxic by assay. Its chromatin analysis concludes the taNK branches "represent distinct lineages that converge transcriptionally, while retaining their ancestral chromatin marks" = INDEPENDENT ORIGINS. And the authors state outright: "their exact origin remains unresolved... both circulating and pre-existing tissue-resident NK cells may contribute." (G2: Serger's own GZMK->ENTPD1 directionality is MultiVelo/diffusion-pseudotime/Monocle3 rooted by hand = INF_TRAJECTORY and I credit none of it; only the functional killing result counts here.)

(4) Horowitz NB et al., Sci Transl Med 2026;18(848):eadw5567, PMID 42090477 — inverts the endpoint again, from the opposite direction. CD39+CD49a+CD103+ cytotoxic trNK differentiated EX VIVO FROM PERIPHERAL NK show "superior cytolytic activity against tumor target cells, enhanced capacity to infiltrate into solid tumor microenvironments, and augmented ability to control solid tumor growth in vivo compared with conventionally activated peripheral NK cells." Where the peripheral-NK -> tissue-resident-tumour-NK transition has actually been produced experimentally, the product is MORE functional, not dysfunctional. (Class: INF_INVITRO for the transition.)

(5) Park MD et al., Nat Immunol 2023, PMID 37081148 (cited by Liu et al. themselves) — reframes the tumour NK deficit as a NUMBERS problem, not a conversion. TREM2+ monocyte-derived macrophages drive NK PAUCITY via IL-18/IL-18BP decoy interactions and reduced IL-15; "Genetic deletion of Trem2 rescued NK cell accumulation and enabled an NK cell-mediated regression of lung tumors." A genuine in vivo genetic perturbation showing the state is a consequence of local cytokine deprivation acting on whatever NK are present, reversible by removing the suppressor — not an irreversible differentiation of newly infiltrating cells.

(6) Tang F et al., Cell 2023, PMID 37607536 — 716 patients, 24 cancer types: the tumour-enriched NK population shows impaired anti-tumour function and unfavourable prognosis, but the mechanism advanced is myeloid (LAMP3+ DC) REGULATION of NK function, again not lineage conversion of newly infiltrating cells.

VERIFICATION OF THE PRIOR AUDITOR'S ITEMS: Sojka 2014 (PMID 24714492 / PMC3975579) confirmed verbatim from the archived full text — "in parabiotic mice, the host liver contains CD49a+ DX5- NK cells of host origin and circulating CD49a- DX5+ NK cells derived from both host and the other parabiont." The Gao 2017 Author Correction (PMID 38514890) confirmed to EXIST by title; the archived record is abstract-only and does NOT contain the quoted "fabricated" wording, so I did not independently re-verify that text and neither should downstream users without pulling the publisher notice.

SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND (G3, my own searches, not inherited): no mouse tumour PARABIOSIS experiment tracking blood NK into a tumour ("parabiosis NK cells tumor" returned only PMID 36630911 iNKT17 and PMID 31405974 IL-17/SOCS3, neither on point; "parabiotic mice natural killer tumour infiltration" 0 hits); no intravascular-staining NK tumour-infiltration study (0 hits). I am not asserting these do not exist. Note the failure mode this exposes: my query "photoconversion Kaede NK cell tumor" ALSO returned 0 PubMed hits, yet the definitive Kaede tumour-NK paper (PMID 38267402) exists and was already sitting in this repo. A G3-compliant "searched and not found" can still be wrong when the index fails.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
I searched the CD8 T cell / TRM, ILC and myeloid literatures on the same structural question. All three deliver a methodological verdict, and they converge: the assays that discriminate recruitment-plus-conversion from selection of a pre-existing pool are an ORIGIN LABEL plus REPEATED SAMPLING OVER TIME. Liu 2026 has neither. Dean 2024 has both.

RECRUITMENT VERSUS RESIDENCY — THE TRM FIELD OWNS THE METHOD.
Snyder ME et al., Sci Immunol 2019;4(33):eaav5581, PMID 30850393 / PMC6435356. HLA-DISPARATE HUMAN LUNG TRANSPLANT with LONGITUDINAL airway sampling: donor and recipient T cells separated by HLA allotype and tracked over time in the same patient. Result: "Donor T cells persist specifically in the lungs (and not blood) of transplant recipients and express high levels of TRM signature markers including CD69, CD103, and CD49a, whereas lung-infiltrating recipient T cells gradually acquire TRM phenotypes over months in vivo." Three lessons for X2. First, this is the human design Liu et al. lack entirely — an allogeneic ORIGIN marker (not a clone marker) plus repeat sampling; Liu's mtDNA barcode marks a clone shared with an upstream ancestor and carries no compartment-of-origin information, and there is exactly one timepoint. Second, when the right method is applied BOTH mechanisms are true simultaneously — pre-existing tissue cells persist AND blood-derived cells convert — which is precisely why a single cross-sectional clonal-sharing statistic cannot apportion them and why the canonical alternative can never be excluded by Liu's design. Third, the conversion took MONTHS in human lung, against Dean's ~72 h in mouse tumour; the tumour timescale is a genuinely different regime and should not be assumed from the TRM literature. The same field also supplies the mouse standard Liu and Dean both omit for vascular contamination: Anderson KG et al., Nat Protoc 2014, PMID 24385150, intravascular staining to discriminate vascular from tissue leukocytes — never applied in either paper, and directly relevant because a "tumour" NK in a dissociated tumour may be an intravascular NK.

THE SAME BARCODE LOGIC, DONE CORRECTLY, IN THE T CELL FIELD.
Yost KE et al., Nat Med 2019, PMID 31359002 — cited by Liu et al. themselves. Clonal replacement of tumour-specific T cells after PD-1 blockade was established with TCR clonotypes as the barcode PLUS PAIRED PRE- AND POST-TREATMENT BIOPSIES. Same inferential structure Liu attempt, but with two timepoints. This is the cleanest demonstration that the barcode is not the evidence; the second timepoint is. It also delivers a substantive result for X2's premise: intratumoural exhausted T cell clones after therapy are largely NEW arrivals rather than reinvigorated residents — i.e. in the T cell field the recruitment model won, but only once someone sampled twice.

EXHAUSTION — THE HOME FIELD HAS FORMAL CRITERIA AND X2'S ENDPOINT MEETS NONE OF THEM.
Blank CU et al., "Defining 'T cell exhaustion'," Nat Rev Immunol 2019;19:665-674, PMID 31570879 / PMC7286441. Eighteen experts, and the article exists precisely because they could not agree on one definition, "ranging from complete lack of effector function to altered functionality to prevent immunopathology." Two exports bear hard on X2. (i) "Dysfunctional" is not a measurable endpoint without a declared assay panel. Liu 2026 ran no NK functional assay of any kind — no cytotoxicity, degranulation, cytokine production or inhibitory-receptor protein — so X2's endpoint has no operational definition in the audited source at all. Dean 2024 by contrast declares and measures a panel (CCL5, IFN-gamma, granzymes A/B/C, perforin, CD107a, 4 h killing) — and that panel shows a SWITCH, not uniform loss (granzymes B and C go UP), which under the consensus's own logic disqualifies the simple word "dysfunctional". (ii) The field's settled architecture is that the terminal exhausted state DERIVES FROM A SELF-RENEWING TCF1+ PROGENITOR resident in the tissue, TOX-enforced epigenetically. That is the canonical "pre-existing subset" alternative, formalized and won in the better-characterized lineage — and it is the structure Serger 2026's independent-chromatin-origin result echoes in NK. The same reference set supplies two further direct blows: Simoni Y et al., Nature 2018, PMID 29769722, bystander CD8 T cells are abundant and phenotypically distinct in human tumour infiltrates; and Scheper W et al., Nat Med 2019, PMID 30510250, low and variable tumour reactivity of the intratumoural TCR repertoire. Together: a large fraction of lymphocytes inside a tumour arrived from blood and did NOT acquire the dysfunctional program. PRESENCE IN TUMOUR IS NOT CONVERSION — which is exactly the inference Liu's "smaller fractions were present in tumor, indicating their ability to infiltrate tissue" makes.

MYELOID — THE FIELD THAT ALREADY MADE THIS EXACT MISTAKE, AND WHOSE RESULT LIU ET AL. ARE ACTUALLY REPORTING.
Liu Z et al., "Fate Mapping via Ms4a3-Expression History Traces Monocyte-Derived Cells," Cell 2019, PMID 31491389. The monocyte-to-tissue-macrophage question was settled only by a constitutive GENETIC FATE MAP of monocyte history, after decades in which marker similarity and in vitro differentiation had licensed the wrong dogma; parabiosis and fate mapping then showed most resident macrophages are embryonically seeded and locally self-renewing. The sting is that Liu et al. 2026's OWN headline claim (circulating monocyte -> intratumoural DC3/macrophage) rests on cross-sectional clonal relatedness — the evidence class the myeloid field explicitly rejected as insufficient. If that is not adequate for their main result, it is a fortiori not adequate for two NK clones in one donor in a supplemental panel.

NET VERDICT THE THREE FIELDS DELIVER ON X2: cross-sectional clonal relatedness establishes shared ancestry and nothing more; an origin label plus a second timepoint is the minimum. Liu 2026 fails that bar and should not carry X2. Dean 2024 clears it in mouse (site-specific photo-label = origin/time label; 5/24/48/72 h chase = repeat sampling; i.v. transfer = origin control). Buggert 2025 clears it in human but for non-tumour tissue and with a different answer (transient residency, lymphatic egress, CD56dim vascular-constrained). The honest position is that X2 is well-evidenced in mouse tumours and unevidenced in human tumours.

The auditor wrote: "Nothing else in the repo currently assumes X2 is TRUE (it is a screen target, not a premise), which is why this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH." I grepped X2 across the repo and that is wrong on its face. X2 is a node with THREE inbound dependency edges inside this screen's own audit graph, all written by sibling auditors:
- /home/user/aaa/phaseA/X4.json, downstream_dependency: Serger 2026 "is also the concrete instance backing claims X1 ... and X2 ..., which assume intratumoural NK states are connected by local differentiation."
- /home/user/aaa/phaseA/X5.json, downstream_dependency: "X5 also underwrites X2 ('Newly infiltrating NK -> dysfunctional tumour NK') and supplies the interpretive frame for X4's ENTPD1+ 'effector/exhausted' end state and for T4."
- /home/user/aaa/phaseA/R2.json, downstream_dependency: "R2's resolution constrains T4 ... and X2, because the Nat Commun 2024 CD49a+ 'tumour-retained' state is the same population both claims argue over." That row NAMED the correct primary source for X2 and the X2 auditor still did not follow the pointer.

CONCRETE NAMED EXECUTABLE DEPENDENCY (verified, and sharpened). /home/user/aaa/scripts/phaseC_power.py lines 162-163: verdict("X2 blood vs tumour (lung)", ("blood","tumour"), lung) and verdict("X2 blood vs tumour (ovarian)", ("blood","tumour"), ovar), gated by the preregistered constants MIN_NK=30, MIN_DONORS=3, MIN_COV=20.0 (lines ~34-36), running over GSE302113 and writing /home/user/aaa/out/T4_power.tsv. Current state: lung arm PASSES with 4 donors (SU-L-003 fails, 0 tumour NK), ovarian arm FAILS with 1 donor (only SU-O-005 clears 30 NK in both compartments). Three consequences, the first two mine:
(1) THE GATE IS POINTED AT THE WRONG DATASET. GSE302113 is Liu 2026, which I have now shown supports nothing about X2. The claim's real evidence is a mouse photoconversion experiment (PMID 38267402) that this gate cannot touch. A phaseC run will produce a number for X2 from a dataset that is not X2's evidence base.
(2) IF IT RUNS ANYWAY, DEPTH-MATCHING IS NOT SUFFICIENT. The prior auditor's handoff said "downsample or depth-match NK cells per compartment." That does not fix the defect. The confound is a MIS-SPECIFIED NULL: Liu's enrichment is a Fisher's exact test "against overall tissue site distribution," i.e. the all-cell-type marginal, so any NK-dominated clone inherits NK's compositional site skew (SU-L-005: blood 1.79x, tumour 0.20x; and reciprocally SU-O-005 tumour 1.90x, which is why the "oligoclonal tumour NK expansion" lands in that donor). It is further confounded by FACS gate design that varies by donor and compartment (SU-L-005 blood = dedicated CD3- library, tumour = CD45+CD3-/CD45- pooled with stroma; SU-L-003 blood = CD56+ sort, tumour unsorted). Any phaseC X2 statistic must be computed against a CELL-TYPE-MATCHED, SORT-GATE-AWARE null, not merely a depth-matched one.
(3) It would also be circular: it re-interrogates the same 10 donors, variants and clone calls that produced the original supplemental observation.

THE REGISTRY VALUE IS NOW WRONG AND WILL PROPAGATE. /home/user/aaa/phaseA/claims.json records X2 as "ESSENTIALLY NO EVIDENCE". Given Dean 2024, the correct entry is "OBS_DIRECT in mouse tumours (photo-labelling, n = 5-11 mice per timepoint, replicated across MC38, CT26 s.c. and orthotopic, B16-F10-OVA, EO771, MMTV-PyMT, 4T1, with egress excluded and a splenic-NK transfer control); INF_MARKER only in human." A screen that reports X2 as unevidenced may prioritize new work on a question that already has a well-controlled in vivo answer. That is a real misdirection risk and it is what keeps this at MEDIUM rather than dropping to LOW.

WHY NOT HIGH, stated against my own inclination to inflate. No code in this repo assumes X2 is true; the phaseC gate is a feasibility check that runs and reports either way. The three inbound edges are interpretive framing between audit rows, not computational premises. In the field, if X2 were false the IL-15 rescue rationale would survive (you would be rescuing a different pool); what would collapse is the "target the conversion drivers" programme — and Dean themselves already weakened that from within by testing TGF-beta (Treg depletion), PGE2 (MC38 Ptgs1/2-/-) and HIF-1alpha (Ncr1-iCre x Hif1a-fl/fl) and finding each individually insufficient. MEDIUM is the honest grade; the auditor's argument for it was not.
